text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for `inference-canary` — P1: spike in 5xx from canary rollout. service: inference-api-canary. link: https://pd.example/incidents/INC-1876

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Triggered page to alex (primary) and maya (secondary). Escalation in 8m if unacked.

alex: on it — acking now. seeing error rate ~12% on canary hosts in eu-west-1. :eyes:

maya: acked. pulling logs and perf dashboards. which release tag? sam, any recent deploys?

sam: I kicked the canary for `release/2026-03-hotpatch` at 13:12 UTC (about 4m ago). Only ~10% traffic routed to canary. No alerts in staging.

jordan: paging in traces — tail latency is ok but tail 95/99 errors are spikes with 500s. looks like OOMs in model-serving process (OOMKill).

alex: copying logs from one failing pod:
```
Mar 14 13:16:02 serving-container[pid]: RuntimeError: KVCache allocation failed: out of memory
Mar 14 13:16:02 kernel: OOM killer invoked for process python3 (serving)
```

maya: interesting — release touched cache prefetch/lock code. memory footprint bumped by ~20% in canary. canary hosts have smaller instance type in eu-west-1 variant.

sam: ugh — I missed the per-region instance profile. I can roll forward a patch but prefer rollback if customers impacted.

lina: priority check — customer impact? Any 5xx seen for hosted customers (prod routes)?

alex: currently only canary route (10%) is affected. some customer requests routed via canary returned 500s. estimate ~0.08% of total requests. but a couple customers reported errors via support.

maya: symptom list: OOMs leading to 500s, pod restarts, request timeouts. No data exfil. No config drift.

ops-bot: Automated mitigation suggestion: scale canary to 0 replicas or unroute via traffic-control. Run `rctl serve update traffic inference-api --canary-weight 0`.

alex: doing traffic cut to 0 now. running command:
```
rctl serve update traffic inference-api --canary-weight 0 --reason "oom regress hotpatch"
```

alex: command succeeded. canary traffic now 0%. watch for error rate drop.

maya: verifying metrics — errors drop started ~40s after cut. pods still crashing but less user impact. good call. :thumbsup:

sam: I'm going to start rollback of the canary image to previous stable. guidance: either scale canary replicas to 0 (done) or rollback deployment. I can do `kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-serving --to-revision=12` for canary set. Thoughts?

jordan: rollback ok but let's also collect diagnostics before we delete pods. can we capture `/proc/meminfo` and `pmap` from a crashed pod?

maya: I grabbed one crash log and heap snapshot already (attached to PD incident). will upload to the canary bucket.

sam: initiating rollback of canary revision to stable at 13:23 UTC:
```
kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/inference-serving-canary --to-revision=12
```

alex: PD incident updated: low customer impact after traffic cut; still tracking root cause and mitigation.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: alex acknowledged at 13:17 UTC. PagerDuty: incident set to "under investigation".

pagerduty: Reminder — automatic escalation scheduled at 13:25 UTC if not resolved.

sam: rollback completed, new pods with stable image coming up. health checks passing on 2/3.

maya: verifying memory after rollback — stable image mem footprint matches baseline. no OOMs on new pods.

alex: starting handoff to follow-up oncall. @jordan you're up for postmortem and RCA. I'll be on shift for the next 10m to answer questions.

jordan: taking on post-incident. action items so far:
- Collect canary pod diagnostics and heap dumps (maya)
- Compare memory profiles between release and stable (maya + sam)
- Re-run canary on a larger instance profile in staging to reproduce (sam)
- Update rollout checklist to validate instance profile compatibility (ops)

lina: please prioritize customer comms if support surfaces more reports. Good mitigation — thanks team.

ops-bot: Suggested follow-up label: `sev1-canary-regression`, assign to jordan, deadline: 2026-03-15 18:00 UTC.

alex: closing chat for immediate mitigation. keeping incident thread open for postmortem prep. if anything new, ping in this thread. :lock:

incident-bot: Incident update: canary traffic cut + rollback performed. Customer impact: limited, partial; some customer errors reported but mitigated. Incident moved to "monitoring" state.

jordan: noted. I'll file the postmortem ticket and include timeline, impact numbers, and action owners. tagging relevant folks.

sam: will open a PR with the quick fix and add instance-profile gating to release pipeline.

maya: uploading diagnostics to https://s3.example/redwood-incidents/1876123456/ and attaching to PD.

alex: thanks all. nice fast coordination. :rocket:
